clue.text: Pop article in French newspaper

indicators.note: the word in tells us the article is placed within the French paper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily newspaper
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A soft drink item appears in a Paris daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a verb or music, but it is the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a British word for a fizzy soft drink, such as the sweet lemon-flavoured kind.

clue.text: Rake, a type of hair-tool?

indicators.note: a type of suggests a variant form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rake is described as a sort of comb for the hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool, which fits 'hair-tool', but here it is a womaniser; rearrange HAIRTOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a seducer in an 18th-century play, the word means a libertine.

clue.text: Dance of university entrants' first pair in Spanish resort

indicators.note: in tells us the new letters go inside the resort's name

parts.note: Malaga is a resort on Spain's Costa del Sol

indicators.note: first pair takes the opening two letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Students arriving at a Spanish resort take to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A malaguena is a Spanish folk dance from the Malaga region, akin to a fandango.

clue.text: Foster, a worker in a colony looking after the young

definitions.meaning: to bring up or care for a child

definitions.text: a worker in a colony looking after the young
definitions.meaning: an ant or bee whose job is tending the larvae

explanation.surface: A foster parent is compared to a busy insect caring for its brood.
explanation.definitionFit: To care for a child and the insect caste that tends larvae share one word.

clue.text: Repudiate girl's proof of membership

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the girl's gives DIS
a membership card proves you belong

explanation.surface: A girl's membership card is rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate something is to throw it aside or reject it.

clue.text: Acclaimed female — a quiet shy person, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite finished, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a timid, retiring person is called a mouse

explanation.surface: A celebrated woman is described as a near-timid wallflower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last E of MOUSE, leaving MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acclaimed is widely praised and well known, that is renowned.

clue.text: Close to a description of a hypotenuse

definitions.meaning: the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is its longest edge, so it can be called a long edge

explanation.definitionFit: Next to or beside, and read as three words it describes the long edge of a triangle.

clue.text: Work overtime like Billy Budd, for example?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
read as over time: era is a time, and in a down clue it sits under the work piece

explanation.surface: Someone toils extra hours, much as the sailor in the story did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtime' is printed as one word but must be split as 'over time'; in a down clue 'over' puts the work on top. Billy Budd is an opera by Benjamin Britten.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten's Billy Budd is an example of a stage work sung throughout.

clue.text: Gun-dog colonist left out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is taken away from the colonist

parts.note: a settler is a colonist

explanation.surface: A hunting dog and a pioneer are both left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of hunting dog trained to point out game birds.

clue.text: Threaten one legislator with closure

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
closure is an end

explanation.surface: A politician is warned that his career is about to close.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over menacingly.

clue.text: Lodge doorkeeper left in the middle of a row

indicators.note: in the middle of tells us the letter for left sits inside the word for a row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A porter at the gate has been left stranded halfway along a line.
explanation.walkthrough: In Freemasonry the officer who guards the door of the lodge is called the tiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masonic official who keeps the outer door of a lodge has this title.

clue.text: Sleepy Merchant Navy love to be in water off Cowes

indicators.note: to be in tells us the navy and love letters are placed inside the stretch of water

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight, where Cowes is, and mainland England
MN is the abbreviation for Merchant Navy
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A drowsy merchant sailor and his sweetheart are afloat in the Solent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight, off the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent describes being drowsy, inclined to doze off.

clue.text: Constituents of concrete in a heap

definitions.meaning: the sand and gravel mixed with cement to make concrete
massed together into a whole, as an adjective

explanation.definitionFit: Builders' term for crushed stone in concrete; as an adjective it means collected into one mass.

clue.text: Prayer for mercy?

definitions.meaning: a short blessing said before a meal
clemency or favour freely shown, as in an act of mercy

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a mealtime blessing and divine favour or clemency.

clue.text: Horned antelope after one run in the country

indicators.note: after tells us the antelope comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns

explanation.surface: An antelope chases a single runner across the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation, the island republic west of Britain.

clue.text: Defender of a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for a point in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a cause or belief, so is its champion.

clue.text: Things needed for performances

definitions.meaning: colloquially, the ... are the bits and pieces required for a job

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang it means the stuff required; it also means activities or deeds carried out.

clue.text: Puffer's old theatre angle

parts.note: the Globe was Shakespeare's theatre in London
to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: A smoker visits an Elizabethan playhouse at an odd angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffer's' reads as 'puffer is'; a puffer is a fish that inflates itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffer is a fish that inflates itself, another name for the same creature.

clue.text: Not quite the person, perhaps, to marry a ward of Chancery?

definitions.text: Not quite the person, perhaps, to marry a ward of Chancery?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise
not quite means a letter is missing from the words

explanation.surface: Someone is almost but not quite the right suitor for a girl in court guardianship.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe, the shepherd Strephon is half fairy, so not quite a person, and marries Phyllis, a ward of Chancery. 'Not quite' drops an E from THEPERSON and 'perhaps' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arcadian shepherd in Iolanthe who weds Phyllis, Lord Chancellor's ward.

clue.text: Standard 'ollow sort of promise given

parts.note: par is a standard or norm, as in up to par
the apostrophe shows a dropped H, so this is a hole said with no H, in Cockney style

explanation.surface: A Cockney speaker gives a hollow pledge of the standard kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A hollow is a hole; with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows, it becomes OLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner's word of honour given in return for early release is this kind of pledge.

clue.text: Parrots in European Community gardens?

parts.note: to garden is to hoe, so gardens means hoes

explanation.surface: Tropical birds are kept in EU gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' looks like birds, but here it is a verb meaning repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot words is to repeat them back, as an answering sound does.

clue.text: Illustrious figure going into divan for a cigar.

indicators.note: going into tells us the famous figure is placed inside the bed

parts.note: a divan is a bed, and so is a cot
a hero is a celebrated, admired person

explanation.surface: A celebrity lies on a couch to smoke a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a type of cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: Bright red borders in study

indicators.note: in tells us the borders are placed inside the study

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
rims are edges or borders

explanation.surface: A red trim is found in someone's study.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep, vivid shade of red.

clue.text: Fellow joining the Spanish printers' trade union

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A man from Spain joins the print workers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: In British printing and newspapers, a union branch in a workplace is called a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally a branch of a printers' or journalists' union at one workplace bears this name.

clue.text: Marks announced for his silent roles?

definitions.text: Marks announced for his silent roles?

parts.words: Marks announced for his silent roles?
parts.note: Marks sounds like the surname of a family of comedy brothers, one of whom never spoke on screen

explanation.surface: Someone is graded publicly for playing mute parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marx Brothers were American film comedians; one brother mimed and played the harp without a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx brother famous for never speaking in his films and for playing the harp.

clue.text: Extra-fashionable collar

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A shirt collar is ultra-trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' looks like part of a shirt but is a verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar a suspect is to arrest them, slang for which is to take them in.

clue.text: Switch of musical number

parts.note: Hair is a famous 1960s rock musical
a number is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Someone changes to a different song from a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a verb meaning change, but a switch is also a tress of false hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a length of false hair worn to add bulk, that is a wig or toupee.

clue.text: Bacteriologist's dish of cooked tripe

indicators.note: cooked suggests the word is prepared differently, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lab scientist serves up offal on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petri dish is the shallow glass dish used to culture bacteria.

clue.text: Peel's inns refurbished and cleaned out

indicators.note: refurbished means done up and rearranged, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the name taken as written, apostrophe dropped and its S kept

explanation.surface: Robert Peel's taverns have been done up at ruinous cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cleaned out is to be left without any money, broke.

clue.text: Shirt tail well up the femur

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: well up means high, far above

explanation.surface: A shirt's hem rides high up the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the bone of the upper leg, so the clue names that limb segment by its bone.

clue.text: Enough, material for the full extent of one's body

definitions.meaning: a piece of cloth sufficient for a garment

definitions.text: the full extent of one's body
definitions.meaning: lying at full stretch, as a horse wins by a body

explanation.definitionFit: A cut of cloth for making something, and the measure from head to foot, share this word.

clue.text: Response from one opposed to line being cut

parts.note: someone opposed is an anti

indicators.note: being cut means the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: a phone line, so line means phone

explanation.surface: A protester answers back while the phone line goes dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut' trims the E from PHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphon is a sung response in church, a chant answering another.
